key_insight: The best system linked phenotype concepts to individual patients in full-text biomedical articles with an overall score of 0.7389, exceeding the baseline by 8.37 percentage points.
clinical_relevance: Patient-specific phenotype extraction could support rare disease research and genotype–phenotype analysis, but clinical utility was not evaluated.
method: Recognize phenotype concepts in full-text biomedical literature.
Associate phenotype concepts with specific patients.
Top teams explored biomedical language models, LLMs, and ensemble strategies.
evidence_signal: The benchmark used 200 annotated PatientPheX articles covering 506 patients, 15,193 phenotype mentions, and 5,656 patient–phenotype associations.
watch_item: Patient attribution and phenotype normalization remain challenging, particularly in articles describing multiple patients.
paper_title: Overview of CHIP 2026 Shared Task 1: Patient-Specific Phenotype Concept Recognition in Full-Text Biomedical Literature
